posts.text:
Exclusive: The Cabinet is split over Britain’s future relationship with Europe after the Prime Minister opened  the door to Britain rejoining the European Union, The i Paper can reveal. 

A narrow majority of Andy Burnham's ministers now back a return to bloc, but they are divided over a second referendum, the timing, and whether Labour risks refighting the toxic Brexit wars. 

Most ministers are understood to be coming round to the view that a second referendum will be unavoidable, if only to stop a future Conservative or Reform UK government from reversing the decision. 

“The EU needs to know this is what Britain really wants," one source said familiar with the discussions said. 

The Prime Minister is expected to use the forthcoming UK-EU summit in November as a springboard for a national debate about Britain's place in Europe. 

Story 👇 w/@singharj

Texas GOP Rep. Keith Self introduced a bill Thursday to repeal the State Department's Diversity Immigrant Visa lottery, which offers permanent residency to up to 55,000 applicants annually from countries with lower levels of immigration to the United States.

The Trump administration attempted to end the program last year after the alleged perpetrator behind shootings at Brown University and MIT used it to enter the country. The alleged shooter was a Portuguese national.

posts.name: The Transcript
posts.text:
$META Q3 Earnings: Interesting numbers on Muse AI

— 10M+ users signed up in just six weeks, despite availability being limited to the U.S. and Canada.
— ~25% of users engage daily, more than 2x the initial engagement of Threads.
— 25%+ of users engage in shopping, with an average purchase size exceeding $200.
— Personal productivity (email, calendar management and task automation) and creativity rank as Muse’s second and third most common use cases, respectively.
— Targets a 10x+ improvement in inference cost efficiency over the next 12 months.
— Meta is building compute capacity to serve 1B+ Muse users over the next few years.
— Muse monetization will begin earlier than Meta's traditional playbook, reflecting high inference costs and significant commerce opportunities.
— Meta expects Muse to eventually generate more revenue per U.S. user than its existing Family of Apps
